description: §48.3.1 + §19.8.3 — a HANDLED `?{}` (`!{}` after the terminator) inside a pure `fn` body SHALL fire E-FN-001 exactly as the unhandled one does (`fn/sql-access-reject`): a bare statement `?{…}.get() !{…}`, a declaration `let row = ?{…}.get() !{…}`, and a `return ?{…}.all() !{…}` — one E-FN-001 per `fn`. The handler adds a failure path; it does not make the access pure. Pre-S455 (g-impl1-handled-sql-lowering-defects-s455 item 5) the `!{}` wrapped the statement in a `guarded-expr` the `fn` body walk never descended into, so all three compiled with NO E-FN-001 (fail-open).
rationale: §48.3.1: a `fn` is a pure, deterministic value function and may not perform database operations; a `?{}` block in a `fn` body is E-FN-001 ('fires regardless of the execution context', §33.3). §19.8.3: a `!{}` handler on the query — written after the terminator — handles its failure; nothing in §19.8.3 exempts the query from any other rule.
